corpusSummary: Corpus covers 2026–era social-science work on large language models (LLMs) across health, education, policy, and everyday life. It includes methodological uses as research tools, studies of trust and adoption in human–AI interaction, and assessments of misinformation, safety, and equity. Recurring concerns address ethics, governance, and alignment, while embodied and situated knowledge gaps reveal limits to AI mimicry of human experience. The collection also probes public-participation potential.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and methodological experimentation
themes.description: A broad set of works treats LLMs as analytical collaborators for coding, framing, data extraction, simulations, and governance evaluation, emphasizing validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, adoption, and wellbeing
themes.description: Studies across health, education, work, and daily life examine how people trust, engage with, and are affected by AI, highlighting factors such as presentation style, privacy, embodiment, and perceived humanness.

themes.name: Equity, safety, and governance of AI across domains
themes.description: Papers propose equity-centered governance and safety frameworks for digital health, education, policy, and culture, alongside fairness and ethical considerations in AI-enabled services.

themes.name: Embodiment gaps and situated knowledge limits
themes.description: Research reveals AI limitations in accessing embodied, sensory, cultural, and relational knowledge, questioning AI’s ability to accurately mirror human experiences and practices.
